text:
Emma Chen: quick heads-up — during vuln triage I noticed customer-facing audit events leaking KMS key identifiers in the `resource` string for scoped-token flows. not a full key, but key IDs are surfaced to members in some views 
Rahul Patel: can you paste an example? is this only for scoped tokens or also regular admin tokens?
Emma Chen: scoped tokens. repro steps: issue scoped token for workspace X, perform export via internal API, event generated and sent to customer audit stream contains `context.kms_key_id` and `resource_owner: workspace:X` in plaintext 
Leo Martinez: oof. that allows enumerating key IDs across tenants if someone has member-level audit access.
Olivia Park: what's the intended visibility model again? members see only their tenant events, admins see all? we intentionally limit which fields are shown in customer-facing exports?
Emma Chen: intended = members can see events for their tenant only, and sensitive KMS identifiers should be redacted unless the tenant admin has opted into including key metadata. but current schema doesn't have a neat knob to indicate "sensitive_key_ref" vs "opaque_ref"
Rahul Patel: sounds like we need schema flags plus RBAC enforcement in the export pipeline. two parts: 1) audit schema change to mark fields as sensitive and 2) validation in export service (and UI) to strip/obfuscate unless caller is tenant-admin and the token scope includes `audit:keys:read`
Jesse (prodeng): adding context: we ship audit exports to S3 for customers and also surface events in-console. both paths call the same enrichment pipeline — easy place to gate.
security-bot: flagging incident ticket INC-2026 (sensitivity: medium) and notifying oncall.
Leo Martinez: proposed minimal schema delta:
```json
{
  "event_id": "...",
  "timestamp": "...",
  "actor": {"id": "u-123", "role": "member"},
  "resource": {"type":"export","id":"e-456","owner_tenant":"t-789"},
  "context": {"kms_key_ref": "arn:redwood:kms:us-east-1:123:key/abcd", "kms_key_sensitive": true}
}
```
We add `kms_key_sensitive: true` and a top-level `owner_tenant` for validation.
Olivia Park: agree. also add `actor_scope` field on the event to indicate whether action was taken by a scoped token vs org admin — that'll simplify enforcement in UI.
Rahul Patel: implementation plan:
- schema PR to `audit-schema` with new boolean flags (kms_key_sensitive, actor_scope)
- export-service change to consult caller scope + tenant membership to redact kms refs
- console: redact in-flight and on historical views unless permissions present
- add regression tests + contract tests between enrichment and export pipeline
Emma Chen: and KMS integration note: make sure we never log full key material. just ID/alias but treat ID as sensitive by default. also confirm KMS audit logs (customer-managed) are not correlated in a way that leaks across tenants.
Jesse (prodeng): risk: customer-facing S3 exports already delivered to some customers. we should run a quick search for recent exports containing "arn:redwood:kms" and notify affected accounts if needed.
Leo Martinez: I'll run a narrow grep on the last 30 days and report findings. assigning to me — will post results here. :mag:
Olivia Park: I'll draft the schema PR and include migration notes + a migration plan for archived events (we can re-run the redaction job for older exports before notifying customers).
Rahul Patel: I'll own the export-service gating and unit tests. will open a PR and tag @Emma for review.
Emma Chen: thanks. action items: Leo run grep, Olivia schema PR, Rahul export gating PR, Jesse coordinate customer comms if we find leaks. timeline: aim for initial PRs by EOD tomorrow.
security-bot: reminder — create audit regression test: make a token with limited `audit:read` and validate exported payloads do not contain `kms_key_ref`.
Jesse (prodeng): noted. I'll prepare a customer communication draft if we need it, lean on legal if we end up notifying.
Leo Martinez: quick update — grep started, found 2 exports (s3 keys) from last 7 days that contain `kms:` substring. investigating tenant mapping now.
Olivia Park: thanks. keep channel updated and add any sensitive findings to the incident ticket.
Emma Chen: feel free to ping me if you need quick HSM/KMS policy context.
Rahul Patel: one more edge-case — internal service-to-service calls using service tokens sometimes bypass scope checking. I'll add a policy check to the token verifier to normalize `actor_scope` for those flows.
Emma Chen: perfect. grateful for quick triage. :thumbsup:
Leo Martinez: will report results by 2pm PST tomorrow. :clock2:
Olivia Park: PR branch `audit/kms-redact-2026` coming up.
security-bot: incident INC-2026 updated: state=investigating, severity=medium, owner=eng-security
Emma Chen: closing loop: we'll review changes in weekly security sync once PRs are open. thanks everyone.
